official.deadline_note: Each higher education institution sets its own admission deadlines in its online recruitment system; applicants must register with the university within those institutional deadlines regardless of the NAWA call deadline.
official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 academic year - Call for applications no 19/2026 of 30 April 2026
official.status_note: The 2026/2027 call (no 19/2026 of 30 April 2026) closed on 29 May 2026 and its results were to be announced by 31 July 2026; NAWA's Call results page now publishes the list of selected candidates for the 2026 Programme. A call for the 2027/2028 academic year had not been announced as of the verification date - NAWA runs one call per academic year and announces the next one on the programme page.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Programme provides for tuition-free education at public higher education institutions; at non-public academic higher education institutions supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education, financial conditions are determined by those institutions and any tuition exemption must be agreed individually between the Scholarship Holder and the institution.
benefits: Monthly scholarship of PLN 2,000 for the standard duration of second-cycle (Master's) degree studies
Exemption from tuition fees at public higher education institutions
One-time lump-sum allowance covering international travel costs related to arrival in Poland for the purpose of undertaking studies under the Programme

Choice of university and field of study from the educational offer of academic higher education institutions supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that have concluded a framework agreement with NAWA
eligibility: Citizenship of one of the listed countries: Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Chile, Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Greece, Spain, the Netherlands, Ireland, Iceland, Israel, Japan, Canada, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Latvia, Malta, Germany, Norway, New Zealand, Portugal, the Republic of Korea, Romania, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, Switzerland, Sweden, Uruguay, the United States of America, Hungary, the United Kingdom, Italy, or residency in Hong Kong, Macau or Taiwan
Not holding Polish citizenship and not having applied for Polish citizenship
First-cycle (Bachelor's) degree obtained in a Programme country no earlier than 2024, or final-year first-cycle student obtaining the degree by 15 July 2026
Plan to commence full-time second-cycle (Master's) degree studies in Poland in the 2026/27 academic year
No previous scholarship from the Director of NAWA under NAWA second-cycle degree programmes
Documented proficiency of at least B2 in Polish (for Polish-taught studies) or in English (for English-taught studies)
requirements: Registration in the online recruitment systems of the higher education institutions within the deadlines set by those institutions
Application submitted exclusively in electronic form via the Agency's ICT system
Application prepared in Polish or English; maximum of one application per Applicant
Documents submitted as scans of original documents or documents signed with a qualified electronic signature
Conclusion of a scholarship agreement no later than 30 days from the date it is made available in the NAWA ICT system
Annual report on education submitted each year, no later than 31 October
documents: Passport page containing personal data (an identity card may be submitted by citizens of European Union Member States)

First-cycle (Bachelor's) degree diploma obtained no earlier than 2024 together with the diploma supplement listing all completed courses and grades; final-year students submit the model certificate issued by their institution
Document confirming proficiency in the language of planned study - compliant with Annex No. 3 (Polish) or Annex No. 4 (English) to the Call

Motivation letter in Polish or English addressing the Applicant's objectives and academic interests, the justification for the chosen field of study and institution, the justification of the selected Master's thesis topic or planned research, and the anticipated impact on further development
Optionally, other documents confirming outstanding achievements
Certified translations into Polish or English for any documents issued in another language, certified by a sworn translator or by a Polish diplomatic or consular mission
selection_criteria: Formal evaluation verifying whether the application meets the formal criteria of the Call
Substantive (merit-based) evaluation of the application content and attachments, with possible interviews
Criterion 1 - arithmetic mean grade from first-cycle studies converted to the Polish grading system (up to 50 points)
Criterion 2 - substantive coherence of the planned educational path, documented in the motivation letter and other documents (up to 50 points)
Positive substantive evaluation requires at least 60 points in total, including no fewer than 25 points under each criterion
Scholarships awarded to Applicants who obtain the highest substantive evaluation scores
coverage: Monthly scholarship of PLN 2,000 paid for the standard duration of studies, for a maximum of 12 months per academic year (up to 5 months in the winter semester and 7 months in the summer semester), starting from the first month of classes
Exemption from tuition fees at public higher education institutions; fees at non-public academic institutions are agreed individually with the institution

One-time lump-sum allowance for international travel related to arrival in Poland, paid once together with the first monthly scholarship, at rates from PLN 1,000 to PLN 6,500 depending on the country of origin
Scholarship paid through the higher education institution at which the Scholarship Holder is enrolled
application_method: Confirm citizenship of one of the listed countries or residency in Hong Kong, Macau or Taiwan, and that you do not hold Polish citizenship

Choose a field of study and an academic higher education institution supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that has concluded a framework agreement with NAWA (list annexed to the Call)
Register in the online recruitment system of the chosen institution and apply for admission independently of NAWA, within its deadlines
Submit the scholarship application electronically via the Agency's ICT system, in Polish or English, attaching the required documents
If awarded, conclude the scholarship agreement within 30 days of it being made available in the NAWA ICT system
official.application_route: Online only: apply through NAWA's ICT system (application in Polish or English, one application maximum) while separately applying for admission at the chosen university - NAWA does not mediate in admission.
official.citizenship_residency: Addressed to foreigners - citizens of 43 listed countries or residents of Hong Kong, Macau or Taiwan; Applicants must not hold Polish citizenship and must not have applied for Polish citizenship.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship offer is addressed exclusively to foreign nationals from the listed countries and territories; Polish citizens are excluded.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Studies must be taken at academic higher education institutions supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that have concluded a framework agreement with NAWA; the Programme does not provide for a call for applications for fields of study offered by HEIs supervised by other ministries.
official.research_requirement: The motivation letter must include the justification of the selected topic of the Master's thesis or planned research.
official.duration: Standard duration of full-time second-cycle (Master's) degree studies; the scholarship is paid for a maximum of 12 months per academic year (up to 5 months in the winter semester and 7 months in the summer semester), starting from the first month of classes.
official.description: The Poland My First Choice NAWA programme aims to encourage young talented people from countries with a high level of socio-economic development to pursue education at Polish academic higher education institutions that have concluded a framework agreement with NAWA, by offering scholarships for second-cycle (Master's) degree studies. Applicants select the university and field of study independently, and NAWA does not act as an intermediary in admission.
official.program_type: Government scholarship programme funded from the State budget
official.english_requirement: Documented proficiency in English at a minimum level of B2 when commencing second-cycle studies conducted in English; accepted documents are those listed in Annex No. 4 to the Call (List of recognized English language certificates). For Polish-taught studies, a minimum level of B2 in Polish is required (Annex No. 3).

not_confirmed: Deadline and dates for the next (2027/2028) call - not yet published on NAWA's pages as of the verification date
verification.notes: All figures taken from the official 2026 Call announcement PDF (no 19/2026 of 30 April 2026) on nawa.gov.pl, cross-checked against the programme's about page and the Call results page; the PLN 2,000 monthly scholarship, tuition exemption at public HEIs and travel allowance rates are all published in section 2.8 of the announcement.

applicant_utility.summary: The Poland My First Choice NAWA scholarship pays PLN 2,000 per month for the standard length of your Master's, waives tuition at public academic universities, and adds a one-off arrival travel payment of PLN 1,000-6,500 depending on your country of origin. You must win two races at once: admission at one of the academic universities that holds a framework agreement with NAWA, decided by that university on its own timetable, and the NAWA award itself. The most recent round, for the 2026/27 academic year, closed on 29 May 2026 and its results are already published, so treat the programme page as the place to watch for the next announcement. Eligibility is narrow: citizenship of one of 43 listed countries (or Hong Kong, Macau or Taiwan residency), a bachelor's degree from 2024 or later, and B2 proficiency in the language your programme is taught in.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent bachelor's graduates from 2024 onwards from any of the 43 listed countries who want an English- or Polish-taught Master's in Poland and can run a university admission application in parallel with the scholarship application.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your country is on the announced list (or that you are a Hong Kong, Macau or Taiwan resident) and that you hold no Polish citizenship and have never applied for it
Check the year of your first-cycle degree - it must be 2024 or later; final-year students must hold it by 15 July 2026 and use the Call's model certificate format
Pick an academic HEI supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that appears on the framework-agreement list annexed to the Call, and note its own admission deadline
Obtain a B2 certificate in the language of instruction from the recognised certificate lists annexed to the Call
Draft the motivation letter in Polish or English covering all four required points, including the justification of your Master's thesis topic
Arrange sworn or consular certified translations for any document not in Polish or English before the deadline
common_rejection_risks: Bachelor's degree awarded before 2024, or final-year status without the properly sealed model certificate
Choosing a university that is not on the framework-agreement list annexed to the Call, or a field taught only at HEIs supervised by other ministries
A language certificate that is not on the recognised annex lists or below B2
A motivation letter that omits one of the four required elements, leaving the substantive score below the 25-point minimum for that criterion
A grade point average that converts to below the Polish 3.55 band, which scores zero points and ends the substantive evaluation outright
Missing the university's own admission deadline because the NAWA deadline got all the attention
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and personal costs beyond the PLN 2,000 monthly scholarship; tuition at non-public academic universities, which is not waived and must be agreed with the institution; the fixed lump-sum travel allowance may not cover the full cost of your flight and moving expenses.
document_audit: The diploma supplement must list every completed course with its final grade, not just the overall result

If you have not yet graduated, the institution-issued certificate must contain your name, the institution and programme names, the completion date, the GPA together with the maximum possible GPA on that scale, the institutional seal or electronic signature, and the signature of the authorized person
Translations must be certified by a sworn translator or by a Polish diplomatic or consular mission; ordinary translations are rejected
EU citizens may submit an identity card page instead of a passport page
alerts: The 2026/27 round closed on 29 May 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Warsaw time; NAWA runs one call per academic year, so monitor the programme page for the 2027/28 announcement rather than relying on stored dates
Institutional admission deadlines run on the university's schedule and can be earlier than the NAWA deadline - apply for admission first
Only one application per Applicant is accepted, so your choice of university and field is effectively your one shot per round
The scholarship agreement must be concluded within 30 days of it being made available in the NAWA ICT system, or the award is lost
Annual reports are due every year by 31 October, and students starting in the summer semester submit a semester report first
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You submit electronically through NAWA's ICT system in Polish or English while independently registering for admission in the chosen university's own online system; if selected, the scholarship agreement is signed in the ICT system and payments flow through your university.
